commit_budget.note: Each order allows ONE code-bearing commit plus an optional documentation-only closeout. R5 used three and R6 has used six, so the budget is breached under BOTH: nine CODE-BEARING commits stand inside r5_baseline..evidence_commit, and four of the nine failed their own exact-SHA run. THE RANGE HOLDS TEN COMMITS AND ONLY NINE OF THEM ARE COUNTED. d0b9924 is documentation-only — five documents, no code — and a budget on code-bearing commits is not spent by a commit that carries none. Its run was RED and is recorded in full beside it; charging it to the budget would overstate the breach, and a budget figure wrong in the direction of severity is still wrong. That is also why the field is named commits_in_the_measured_range rather than code_bearing_commits: the gate checks it against git rev-list --first-parent so it must hold EVERY commit in the range, and code_bearing decides which ones count. THE AGGREGATE ONCE STOPPED AT THREE, and that was an undercount produced by the record's own shape: the range ends at the evidence commit, so every commit made after the last GREEN run fell outside it and was recorded nowhere — the same 'lists fewer commits than the history holds' defect R5 was rejected for, reproduced inside the field built to disclose it. commits_ahead_of_the_evidence_commit closed it and the gate checks that list against git in both directions. Each successor commit exists to close a failure rather than to add scope — that is the explanation and it is not a defence, and the architect has ruled that disclosure does not cure the breach. R6 §5's verbatim text is NOT held in this repository (docs/orders/FBL-020-R6.md Part 2 marks it derived), so its budget is applied on the same terms as R5 §5 and is reported, not construed.

this_commit.why_it_has_no_sha_here: A record cannot name the SHA of the commit that contains it: the SHA does not exist until the commit is written, and writing it changes the SHA. This commit is the FBL-020-R6 §5 DOCUMENTATION-ONLY closeout — documents and this record, no code, no test, no migration — so it is NOT code-bearing and does not move commit_budget.used. THAT CLAIM IS CHECKED, NOT TAKEN ON TRUST: scripts/check-final-state.ts reads the paths HEAD changed, wherever git can answer, and refuses this declaration over any path outside docs/ and root Markdown. The check exists because the claim was once made falsely — a closeout authored as documentation-only and committed carrying scripts/ and tests/ — and nothing looked. The declaration still drives the arithmetic, because a shallow clone has no parent to diff against and the tree copy with no .git that scripts/mutation-kill.ts runs its batteries inside has nothing at all, so the budget comes out the same in every environment and is bound to reality wherever reality is readable. LIKE repository_head_relation, BOTH DESCRIBE THE COMMITTED STATE: run in the working tree before this closeout exists, the cross-check reads the paths of whatever is currently HEAD — the gate being right about the wrong commit — and the head relation reads the tree without this commit in it. Neither arises in CI, where a run checks out the commit under test. The working procedure is to re-run the gate and the documentation battery AFTER committing and BEFORE pushing, and the exact-SHA run recorded against this closeout is what a reader should check.
